chunks: By this chain of narration, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Ali ibn Hilal al-Ahmasi, he said: Sharik narrated to us from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, who said:

Al-Hajjaj sent for Yahya ibn Ya'mur and said to him: Are you the one who claims that the two sons of Ali are the sons of the Messenger of God? He said: Yes, and I can recite to you from the Quran regarding that. He said: Give it. He said: Grant me protection. He said: Protection is yours.

He said: Does not God, Mighty and Majestic, say: "We bestowed upon him Ishaq and Ya'qub, each We guided; and Nuh We guided before, and from his descendants Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa, and Harun - and thus We reward the doers of good"? Then he said: "And Zakariyya, Yahya, and 'Isa" - did 'Isa have a father? He said: No.

He said: Yet God, Mighty and Majestic, attributed him in the scripture to Ibrahim. He said: What caused you to narrate such a hadith? He said: The covenant God took from the scholars regarding their knowledge - that they should not conceal knowledge they have learned.

key_terms.ابني علي: The two sons of Ali - referring to al-Hasan and al-Husayn, sons of Ali ibn Abi Talib and Fatima bint Muhammad
key_terms.الامان: Guarantee of safety/protection - a formal pledge of safety in Islamic tradition
key_terms.ذرية: Progeny/descendants - key Quranic term for lineage, including through maternal line
key_terms.يكتموا علما: Conceal knowledge - echoing the Quranic prohibition in 3:187 against scholars hiding truth

ai.seo_question: Are al-Hasan and al-Husayn considered the sons of the Prophet Muhammad in the Quran?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts a bold confrontation between the scholar Yahya ibn Ya'mur and the tyrannical Umayyad governor al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf (d. 95 AH), who terrorized the scholars of Iraq. When al-Hajjaj challenged Yahya's claim that al-Hasan and al-Husayn were the sons of the Prophet, Yahya cited Quran 6:84-85 where 'Isa (Jesus), who had no father, is counted among Ibrahim's descendants - proving that maternal lineage is valid in Quranic genealogy. When pressed about why he dared speak such truth to power, Yahya invoked God's covenant that scholars must not conceal their knowledge.

en.bilal-muhammad: By this isnad from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi from `Ali b. Hilal al-Ahmasi. He said: Sharik narrated to us from `Abd al-Malik b. `Umayr.

He said: Al-Hajjaj sent for Yahya b. Ya`mur, and he said to him: Are you the one that alleges that the two sons of `Ali are the sons of the Messenger of Allah? He said: Yes, and I could recite that from the Quran for you. He said: Give it. He said: Grant me protection. He said: Protection is yours.

He said: Doesn’t Allah say, “We bestowed him with Ishaq and Ya`qub, and We guided all of them. And Nuh, We guided before; and among his descendants, Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa, and Harun – thus We reward the doers of good” [6:84]? Then, he said, “And Zakariyya, Yahya, and `Isa” [6:85] – did `Isa have a father? He said: No.
He said: Yet Allah attributed him to Ibrahim in the scripture. He said: What caused you to narrate this? He said: Allah did not command the scholars to conceal knowledge from being taught.
